To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Niuxinshan Intrusive Complex (NIC) is the main source of the hydrothermal fluids that formed the Huajian gold deposits.

the NIC’s geochemistry and geochronology indicate that the NIC formed in a volcanic-arc setting and that the mineralization in this area is Late Jurassic (~ 155 Ma) and is genetically related to the NIC’s crystallization of its shallow crust-sourced portions.
the Huajian gold mineralization is genetically related to the Late Jurassic (155 Ma) shallow-crustal-sourced portion of the Niuxinshan complex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the timing of mineralization in the Huajian gold district and the tectonic setting of the NIC.
the tectonic evolution and metallogenesis of the northern margin of NCC after ~155 Ma.
the geological significance of the Niuxinshan gold deposit, and provides a new understanding of the tectono-thermal evolution and metallogeny associated to the northern margin of NCC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this mineralization was generated in a post-collisional environment, and that it was associated with the subduction and closure of a paleo-Tethys Ocean.

the Huajian gold district was formed during the Late Jurassic, in a continental convergent setting, and that its formation is related to the crystallizing of the shallow crust-sourced portions of the NIC.

the mineralization in the Huajian gold district was related to the tectonic transition between a thickened arc and a thinned intra-plate setting, with the NIC’s shallow crustal-sources playing a critical role.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the mineralization of the Huajian gold district was formed in an extensional environment in response to the subduction and collision of the Paleo-Pacific Plate and the North China Plate.
the NIC is a typical example of the metallogenic system associated with convergent margins in the northern NCC.

the Huajian gold deposits formed in the northern margin in the NCC in the late Mesozoic, which was a transitional period for the tectonism and metallogeny of the NCC, from an intra-plate setting with a thin crust and a low geothermal gradient to a convergent setting with a thick crust and a high geothermal gradient.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the mineralization in the northern margin is related to the subduction of the Paleo-Pacific plate and the subsequent collision of the NCC with the Siberian Craton, which resulted in the development of the Early–Middle Jurassic volcanic arcs in the eastern NCC and the Late Jurassic–Early Cretaceous postcollisional extensional environment in the northern margin.
the NIC represents a typical example of convergent margin magmas in an intra-plate setting.

the tectonic setting of this area changed from a convergent setting to an intra-plate setting at 185 and 155 Ma, respectively, and that the Huajian gold deposits were formed in a shallow crustal-sourcing environment during the intra-plate stage.
